report_name: Children's Foundation Data Breach Occurs via Third-Party IT Provider

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Actor
threat_actors.description: An unauthorized party that gained access to the network of Highland Shores Children's Aid Society, encrypted systems in a ransomware-style attack, and exfiltrated data belonging to The Children's Foundation.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The attacker deployed encryption on the systems of the IT provider, Highland Shores Children's Aid Society, to disrupt operations, a tactic characteristic of ransomware attacks.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: The attacker indirectly breached The Children's Foundation by compromising its third-party IT service provider, Highland Shores Children's Aid Society, exploiting the trusted relationship between the two organizations to access the foundation's data.

identities.name: The Children's Foundation
identities.description: A Canadian non-profit organization that was the indirect victim of a data breach. Its data, including personal information of volunteers, donors, and program applicants, was exposed due to a compromise at its third-party IT provider.

identities.name: Highland Shores Children's Aid Society
identities.description: A third-party IT service provider for The Children's Foundation. Its network was breached by an unauthorized actor in July 2026, leading to a ransomware attack and the exposure of client data.

indicators.name: Permission Groups Discovery via whoami
indicators.pattern:
title: Permission Groups Discovery via whoami
id: 9c5a8d7e-1f2a-4b3c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of 'whoami /groups' command, which can be used by attackers for discovery of permission groups on a compromised system.
references:
  - https://www.quintenews.com/2026/11/10/childrens-foundation-data-breach/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-10
tags:
  - attack.t1069
level: low
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\whoami.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/groups'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of 'whoami /groups', a command used for discovering local and domain group memberships, as suggested in the article's hunting hints.
